messages:
alex: Nightly GPU smoke is red on h100-warmup, started ~10m ago. Failing during model warmup, job hangs on a kernel launch. @kevin @maria can you quick-check? :eyes:
infra-bot: Test run 2024-11-12T03:12:00Z — job gpu-nightly/h100-warmup — status: FAILED (step: warmup-loop)

alex: Pasted the failing tail, looks like kernel launch stuck then Xid reported.
```
[2024-11-12T03:11:42Z] warmup: launch_kernel() returned 0x1
[2024-11-12T03:11:43Z] nvml: GPU 0: ECC
[2024-11-12T03:11:44Z] kernel: VA_SPACE: launching attention kernel batch=1
[2024-11-12T03:11:45Z] dmesg: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID 12345
```

maria: Thx. Two quick q's: did this start after the driver bump last night? and can you paste `nvidia-smi -q` from the host?

alex: Driver bump to 535.86 rolled last night on the pool. nvidia-smi output:
```
GPU 0: H100
Driver Version: 535.86
CUDA Version: 12.2
Processes: 3
Used GPU Memory: 1.2G
```

kevin: Xid 79 is typical of a kernel timeout/kernel launch fault. Could be driver mismatched with our kernel modules or a bad firmware. Any churn in firmware or kernel package on that image?

jules: Also check if this is only happening on this host or across multiple shards. If it's just one node, might be flaky hardware or a transient preemption.

alex: I only see the failure on shard-07 and shard-10 of this matrix. shard-11 passed. So not universal.

maria: Ok please kick a rerun on just the failed shards and include debug logging (ENV DEBUG=1) so we can see more kernel launch logs. If it repros, we should pin the driver to previous release to compare.

alex: Rerun requested: infra-bot, rerun shards shard-07,shard-10 with debug=1.
infra-bot: Rerun queued — run id 2024-11-12-03-20-51-rerun-482 — estimated start in 30s. :zap:

kevin: If rerun still flakes, I can do a quick bisect between the two nightly images: pre-driver-bump vs post-driver-bump. I can also repro locally on our h100 dev machine with the same image.

infra-bot: Rerun started — shard-07: RUNNING, shard-10: RUNNING

alex: shard-07 log shows same kernel stall at warmup step. dmesg again: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79` and kernel reports `gpu watchdog timeout`.

jules: Sounds like driver/firmware regression. Can you also collect `cat /sys/class/pci_bus/0000:65/device/firmware_version` and `modinfo nvidia`?

alex: Collected and uploaded to artifact: https://artifacts/redwood/nightly/2024-11-12/runs/482/artifacts/ (attached). modinfo shows `nvidia 535.86` modules. firmware_version file shows `0x1a2b`.

maria: Good. For now let's keep the job pinned to the older driver 525.85 for the next scheduled weekend until we triage. I'll open a short infra ticket to revert pool image.

kevin: I'll start a bisect tomorrow morning across our CI images to narrow down the regression commit, focusing on driver package + kernel module builds. If someone can add me to the run, I'll kick off local repro.

alex: Thanks — infra ticket created #INFRA-1723 to revert driver on pool. For immediate unblocking, can we mark the nightly as flaky and notify SRE to avoid paging?

maria: I'll mark the run flaky and silence alerts for the nightly job for 4 hours. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Rerun results: shard-07 FAILED (same hang), shard-10 PASSED. Overall run status: UNSTABLE.

jules: Mixed results — that suggests intermittent hardware/host-level flakiness combined with driver sensitivity. Good to bisect.

alex: cc @kevin — I added you to the artifacts and SSH access to shard-07 host for debugging.

kevin: Got it. I'll start with a live repro then bisect kernel/driver combo. Will update thread when I have a narrowed commit range. :mag:

maria: Thanks all. If bisect points to driver package, we'll roll back and run extended soak on a canary pool.

alex: Closing loop here for now — continuing in infra ticket and with kevin's bisect. :white_check_mark:
